newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU to keep British beef-embargo after mad cow data.
newsitem.headline: EU to keep British beef-embargo after mad cow data.

text.p: The European Union will maintain an embargo on British beef exports after scientists found more evidence the cattle disease could spread to people, Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Thursday.

"What the British scientists have discovered shows how serious the crisis is," he told a news conference. "We must make sure all the measures which have been put in place are maintained, because now we have to face the fact that the disease can be transmitted to people."

The research published on Wednesday found that a new variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans left chemical traces very similar to the brain-wasting cattle disease, known scientifically as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

"(The research) shows that the risk of transmission to humans is a fact -- it is not the proof, but it is one more proof," Fischler said after briefing a French parliamentary committee on the seven-month-old European beef crisis.
Speaking through a French translator, the Austrian-born official said the new evidence merely reinforced a need for measures containing the disease to be fully implemented.

The EU banned British beef exports in March after London first reported a suspected link between mad cow disease and CJD. Britain has said a cull agreed with EU leaders this summer as a way of easing the ban is no longer needed to eliminate BSE.
